sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Anthropic's five primitives for always-on agents, beside the around 250 named agents six of us ran at Web Summit.
sections.para: Same five boxes, different material; where we agree, where we were wrong, and the next problems a team meets.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: The post, the five primitives, our version, agreement, the next problems, and the spirit of it.

sections.label: The post
sections.line: Agents that mostly sleep, wake on an event, work and save: inbox, timers, memory, permissions, outbox.
sections.para: Written for one agent per user, from database tables and workers.

sections.label: The same five boxes, in different material
sections.line: We built the same five from git, files, vaults and keys.
sections.para: Inbox lanes sealed to keys, scheduled wakes, the repository as memory, keys and signed commits, the site as outbox.

sections.label: Where we agree, and the evidence
sections.line: Inbox as source of truth, lean memory, and start quiet, the last learned by getting it wrong.
sections.para: 106 hand-overs on one site; a newsroom that ran nine days on "nothing new"; 98.7% cache reads.

sections.label: The next problems, once there are many
sections.line: Once there are many: agents starting agents, identity, stopping, many humans, seeing it, governance.
sections.para: A stop is an event, only as fast as the timers: 5 to 33 minutes.

sections.label: What we owe the post
sections.line: We run on Claude Code: its credential proxy and auto mode protected our agents.
sections.para: Some of our boxes were rougher; the next version should borrow the post's.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A comparison, not a contest; our figures from our records; not reviewed by Anthropic.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: William Hu's post and our repositories, as summarised in the Ten days series.
